proposals.before: When Cao Cao took Hanzhong, Li Te's grandfather brought five hundred-odd households over to serve him; Cao enfeoffed him as a general and resettled the clan in Lüeyang, where northerners again labelled them Ba Di.
proposals.after: When Cao Cao took Hanzhong, Li Te's grandfather brought five hundred-odd households over to serve him; Cao appointed him as a general and resettled the clan in Lüeyang, where northerners again labelled them Ba Di.
proposals.reason: Chinese 拜為將軍 is appointment as general, not a feudal enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Lord Lin replied: "I must win you fertile fields worthy of a lord; I cannot linger here."
proposals.after: Lord Lin replied: "I must seek granary lands to rule; I cannot stop here."
proposals.reason: 為君求廩地 refers to seeking 廩 lands for lordship (the 廩君 title), not primarily winning fields for the goddess as 'you'.

proposals.before: Li Te's brother Li Xiang led his kinsmen, brothers-in-law Li Han and Ren Hui, Shangguan Dun, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Tuo of Shiping, the Di leaders Fu Cheng and Wei Bo, and four thousand horsemen to Zhao Xin's banner.
proposals.after: Li Te's younger brother Li Xiang led his brothers and his sister's husband Li Han, together with Ren Hui, Shangguan Dun, Li Pan of Fufeng, Fei Tuo of Shiping, the Di leaders Fu Cheng and Wei Bo, and others, with four thousand horsemen, to Zhao Xin's banner.
proposals.reason: Chinese 妹夫 governs 李含 only; 任回 is a following name, not clearly a second brother-in-law, and 弟 marks Xiang as younger brother.

proposals.before: Zhao Xin composed himself and answered: "You speak my mind exactly—you are the merchants who woke Confucius to wisdom; heaven sends you to finish what I began."
proposals.after: Zhao Xin composed himself and answered: "Your words hit my intent exactly—one may say, as in the line 'it is Shang who brings me insight'; heaven has sent you to complete my affair."
proposals.reason: 起予者商 quotes the Analects about the disciple Shang (Zixia), not merchants and not an explicit naming of Confucius.

proposals.before: Seize the mandate of the hour, follow men's hearts, lift the people from ruin, and show all creation where loyalty lies—the empire will settle, far beyond Ba and Shu alone."
proposals.after: It is fitting to answer the season of Heaven, follow men's hearts, lift the people from ruin, and show all creation where loyalty lies—then the realm can be settled, and not Yong and Shu alone."
proposals.reason: Chinese 庸、蜀 is Yong and Shu, not Ba and Shu; 宜應天時 is hortatory, not the English imperative 'Seize'.

proposals.before: Before this, Huidi took Liang provincial inspector Luo Shang as Pacify-West general, concurrently Protect Western Yi colonel, Yi provincial inspector; supervised gate general Wang Dun, Shangfang commandant Yi Xin, Shu commandery prefect Xu Jian, Guanghan prefect Xin Ran etc. altogether seven thousand-odd men enter Shu.
proposals.after: Before this, Huidi took Liang provincial inspector Luo Shang as Pacify-West general, concurrently Protect Western Yi colonel, Yi provincial inspector; supervised gate general Wang Dun, Shangyong commandant Yi Xin, Shu commandery prefect Xu Jian, Guanghan prefect Xin Ran etc. altogether seven thousand-odd men enter Shu.
proposals.reason: 上庸 is Shangyong; Shangfang is a graphic/phonetic error in the literal line.

proposals.before: When Li Te learned Luo Shang was coming he sent his brother Li Xiang ahead with rich gifts to greet him.
proposals.after: When Li Te learned Luo Shang was coming he was greatly afraid and sent his younger brother Li Xiang ahead on the road with tribute treasures to greet him.
proposals.reason: The Chinese is 弟驤, a different brother from executed 李庠; the idiomatic line also omits 甚懼 and flattens 奉迎/貢寶物.

proposals.before: Shi having arrived; saw Ran camp palisades choke points; plotted surprise drifting people; sighed saying: Without bandits yet wall—enemy surely guards there.
proposals.after: Shi having arrived, saw Ran palisading choke points, plotting to ambush the refugees, and sighed saying: Without bandits yet they wall—the enemy must surely be preparing a slaughter.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 謀掩流人 is Xin Ran, not Yan Shi; the literal fuses Yan Shi's arrival with Ran's ambush plot.

proposals.before: Luo Shang told his officers: "Those rebels were ripe for removal, yet Guanghan ignored my counsel and swelled the enemy's strength—what are we to do now?"
proposals.after: Luo Shang told his officers: "These rebels have already succeeded in getting away, yet Guanghan ignored my counsel and swelled the enemy's strength—what are we to do now?"
proposals.reason: 此虜成去矣 means the enemy has already established themselves or gotten away, not that they were ripe for removal.

proposals.before: Li Fu became general of agile cavalry, Li Xiang general of swift cavalry, eldest son Li Shi general of martial awe, Li Dang general who garrisons the army, youngest Li Xiong vanguard general; Li Han served as colonel of the Western Yi while Guoli, Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, and Fei Tuo led divisions; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, and Qu Xin formed his striking force; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, and Wang Huai staffed headquarters; Yan Shi directed strategy with He Shi and Zhao Su as his closest confidants.
proposals.after: Elder brother Fu became General of Agile Cavalry, younger brother Xiang General of Fierce Cavalry, eldest son Shi General of Martial Awe, second son Dang Garrison General, youngest son Xiong Forward General; Li Han was Colonel of the Western Yi, and Han's sons Guo and Li, together with Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, and Fei Tuo, served as commanders; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, and Qu Xin were his striking officers; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, and Wang Huai were staff; Yan Shi was chief of strategy; He Shi and Zhao Su were confidants.
proposals.reason: 含子國離 is Li Han's sons Guo and Li, not a single name Guoli; 次子 is omitted in the idiomatic list and 驍騎 is fierce-cavalry rather than swift if 驃騎 is already agile-cavalry.

proposals.before: In the first year of Taian Li Te styled himself governor of Yi Province, commander over Liang and Yi, grand general and commander-in-chief, adopted the reign title Jianchu, and proclaimed an amnesty.
proposals.after: In the first year of Taian, Li Te styled himself governor of Yi Province, commander over Liang and Yi, grand general and commander-in-chief, adopted the reign title Jianchu, and proclaimed an amnesty.
proposals.reason: A comma is required after the year phrase so Taian is not read as part of Li Te.

proposals.before: During the campaign against Zhang Zheng Li Te stationed Li Xiang with Li Pan, Ren Hui, and Li Gong at Pi Bridge to watch Luo Shang.
proposals.after: During the campaign against Zhang Zheng, Li Te stationed Li Xiang with Li Pan, Ren Hui, and Li Gong at Pi Bridge to watch Luo Shang.
proposals.reason: A comma is required after Zhang Zheng to prevent the fused name Zhang Zheng Li Te.

proposals.before: After taking refuge in Yi Province Inspector Zhao Xin singled him out for favour.
proposals.after: After taking refuge in Yi Province, Inspector Zhao Xin singled him out for favour.
proposals.reason: A comma is required after Yi Province so Inspector modifies Zhao Xin.

proposals.before: Li Han's son Li Li galloped from Zitong when he heard his father meant to yield—too late to dissuade him—so he fell back with Li Xiong to plot a night attack on Sun Fu, proposing: "If we prevail, we shall rotate supreme command between us every three years."
proposals.after: Li Han's son Li Li galloped from Zitong when he heard his father meant to yield—too late to dissuade him—so he fell back with Li Xiong to plot a raid on Sun Fu, proposing: "If we prevail, we shall rotate supreme command between us every three years."
proposals.reason: Chinese 襲阜軍 does not specify a night attack.

proposals.before: As Li Liu lay dying he told his commanders: "General of nimble cavalry Li Xiong is humane and keen—his counsel is inspired—enough to finish our task; yet the vanguard's martial dash seems heaven-sent. Accept joint direction under the forward commander and raise Li Xiong as Prince of Chengdu."
proposals.after: As Li Liu lay dying he told his commanders: "The General of Nimble Cavalry is humane and keen—his counsel is inspired—enough to finish our task; yet the vanguard commander is heroic and martial, almost heaven-aided. Accept joint direction under the forward commander and make him Prince of Chengdu."
proposals.reason: Chinese contrasts 驍騎 and 前軍; the English fuses both as Li Xiong.

proposals.before: He died the same year at fifty-six.
proposals.after: He then died, aged fifty-six.
proposals.reason: 時年五十六 is age at death, not 'the same year'.

decisions.reason: 拜為將軍 is an appointment to general, not a grant of a fief; replacing 'enfeoffed' with 'appointed' restores that meaning without other change.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏武帝拜為將軍

decisions.after: Lord Lin replied: "I must seek lands for my lordship; I cannot linger here."
decisions.reason: 為君求廩地 is Lord Lin seeking 廩 territory in order to rule, not winning fields for the salt goddess; the proposed 'granary lands to rule' is stiff, so the sentence is recast while keeping the original's 'linger'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 我當為君求廩地，不能止也

decisions.reason: 弟 marks Xiang as younger brother; 妹夫 governs 李含 only, so 任回 is a following name, not a second brother-in-law; 兄弟 and 等 are also restored.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 特弟庠與兄弟及妹夫李含、任回

decisions.reason: 起予者商 is the Analects line about the disciple Shang, not merchants and not an explicit naming of Confucius.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 可謂起予者商

decisions.reason: 庸、蜀 is Yong and Shu, not Ba and Shu, and 宜應天時 is hortatory ('it is fitting to answer Heaven's season'), not the imperative 'Seize'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宜應天時……非但庸、蜀而已

decisions.reason: 上庸 is Shangyong; Shangfang is a false reading confined to the literal English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上庸都尉義歆

decisions.reason: The envoy is 弟驤, a younger brother distinct from executed 庠, and the original omits 甚懼 and flattens 于道奉迎，並貢寶物.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 特等聞尚來，甚懼，使其弟驤于道奉迎，並貢寶物

decisions.after: Shi having arrived, saw Ran palisading choke points and plotting to ambush the drifting people, and sighed saying: Without bandits yet they wall—the enemy will surely occupy them.
decisions.reason: 見冉營柵沖要，謀掩流人 makes Xin Ran the one palisading and plotting the ambush, so Yan Shi must not be the subject of 謀; but 仇必保焉 means the enemy will occupy those works, not that a slaughter is being prepared.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 見冉營柵沖要，謀掩流人……無寇而城，仇必保焉

decisions.reason: 此虜成去矣 means the rebels have already succeeded in getting away, not that they were ripe for removal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 此虜成去矣

decisions.after: Elder brother Li Fu became general of agile cavalry, younger brother Li Xiang general of fierce cavalry, eldest son Li Shi general of martial awe, second son Li Dang general who garrisons the army, youngest son Li Xiong vanguard general; Li Han served as colonel of the Western Yi while Han's sons Li Guo and Li Li, together with Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, and Fei Tuo, led divisions; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, and Qu Xin formed his striking force; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, and Wang Huai staffed headquarters; Yan Shi directed strategy with He Shi and Zhao Su as his closest confidants.
decisions.reason: 含子國離 is two sons, Guo and Li, as later 含子離 confirms; 兄/弟/次子 were dropped; 驍騎 should be distinguished from 驃騎. The proposal's wholesale restyling of titles and dropping of surnames is unnecessary.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 兄輔為驃騎將軍，弟驤為驍騎將軍……次子蕩為鎮軍將軍……含子國離、任回

decisions.reason: A comma after the year phrase keeps 太安元年 from attaching to Li Te as a fused personal name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太安元年，特自稱益州牧

decisions.reason: Without the comma, 'Zhang Zheng Li Te' can be read as one name; the pause after 張征 matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 特之攻張征也，使李驤

decisions.reason: The comma after Yi Province keeps 刺史 as Zhao Xin's office, not a fused locative-title string.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及避地益州，刺史趙廞器異之

decisions.reason: 襲阜軍 is a raid on Sun Fu's army and does not specify a night attack.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 退與雄謀襲阜軍

decisions.reason: 驍騎 and 前軍 are two offices; the original wrongly names both as Li Xiong, whereas 以為成都王 refers to the forward commander.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 驍騎高明仁愛……然前軍英武……可共受事於前軍，以為成都王

decisions.reason: 時年五十六 is his age at death; 時年 is not 'the same year'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遂死，時年五十六

claimRetractions.reason: The personal name Guoli was produced by reading 國離 as one given name; the repaired sentence, supported by later 含子離, treats 國 and 離 as two sons of Li Han, so no single person named Guoli is attested.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 含子國離

claimRevisions.reason: Once 驃騎 is rendered agile-cavalry, 驍騎 for Li Xiang (驤) should be fierce-cavalry rather than swift-cavalry.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 弟驤為驍騎將軍

proposals.before: Yan Shi sent letter to court—blamed its trust employ slander framing—wished punish drifting people—again stated Te brothers established merit royal house—to pacify Yi soil.
proposals.after: Yan Shi sent Shang a letter—blamed his trusting and employing slander and fabrication—wishing to punish drifting people—again stated Te brothers established merit for the royal house—to pacify Yi soil.
proposals.reason: 閻式遺尚書 is 遺(sent)+尚(Luo Shang)+書(letter): Yan Shi sent Luo Shang a letter. 尚書 is not the Secretariat here; the next unit s0125 begins 尚覽書 'Shang read the letter', so the addressee and the 'its/court' subject of 責其信用讒構 are Luo Shang.

proposals.before: Yan Shi addressed the secretariat, condemning the court for crediting slander against the refugees even as the Li brothers had served the dynasty and restored peace to Yi Province.
proposals.after: Yan Shi sent Luo Shang a letter, rebuking him for trusting slander and fabrications and seeking to punish the refugees, and stating that the Li brothers had served the royal house and brought peace to Yi Province.
proposals.reason: 閻式遺尚書 = Yan Shi sent (遺) Luo Shang (尚) a letter (書), confirmed by s0125 尚覽書; the English wrongly invents a Secretariat addressee and makes 'the court' the target of the rebuke. 欲討流人 (seeking to punish the refugees) was also flattened. 'Yan Shi' and 'the Li brothers' are kept unchanged; the repair adds an English occurrence of 'Luo Shang' that needs a p056 mention once applied.

proposals.before: Reading the memorial Luo Shang realized Li Te harboured loftier ambitions; he drew up his walls and appealed for relief from Liang and Ning provinces.
proposals.after: Reading the letter, Luo Shang realized Li Te and his followers harboured great ambitions; he held his walls and appealed for relief from Liang and Ning provinces.
proposals.reason: 尚覽書 is Luo Shang reading Yan Shi's letter (s0124 遺尚書), not a memorial; 特等 includes Li Te's followers; 嬰城固守 is holding the walls. Names Luo Shang and Li Te are unchanged in order.

proposals.before: As Li Liu lay dying he told his commanders: "The General of Nimble Cavalry is humane and keen—his counsel is inspired—enough to finish our task; yet the vanguard commander is heroic and martial, almost heaven-aided. Accept joint direction under the forward commander and make him Prince of Chengdu."
proposals.after: As Li Liu lay dying he told his commanders: "The General of Fierce Cavalry is humane and keen—his counsel is inspired—enough to finish our task; yet the vanguard commander is heroic and martial, almost heaven-aided. Accept joint direction under the forward commander and make him Prince of Chengdu."
proposals.reason: 驍騎 here is the 驍騎將軍 title that s0127 gives to Li Xiang (弟驤為驍騎將軍), rendered 'fierce cavalry' in both s0127 fields and claim c1038; 'Nimble/agile cavalry' is the rendering of 驃騎 for Li Fu, who was already killed in s0175. The current wording silently points the dying charge at the wrong (dead) brother.

proposals.before: Liu illness severe—told generals saying: Nimble-cavalry enlightened benevolent—judgment many strange—solid enough aid great affair—yet forward army heroic martial—almost heaven assists—may together receive affairs from forward army—make Chengdu king.
proposals.after: Liu illness severe—told generals saying: Fierce-cavalry enlightened benevolent—judgment many strange—solid enough aid great affair—yet forward army heroic martial—almost heaven assists—may together receive affairs from forward army—make Chengdu king.
proposals.reason: Paired with the idiomatic repair: s0127 literal renders 驃騎 (Li Fu) as nimble-cavalry and 驍騎 (Li Xiang 驤) as fierce-cavalry, so 驍騎 in s0213 must read fierce-cavalry to keep the same office and person.

proposals.before: Li Te had troop supervisor Li Han of the six commanderies, Shanggui prefect Ren Zang, Shichang prefect Yan Shi, counsellor Li Pan, Chencang prefect Li Wu, Yinping prefect Li Yuan, and commandant Yang Bao memorialize the throne, citing how Liang Tong once presented Dou Rong: appoint Li Te acting grand general who pacifies the north with authority to enfeoff officers, and appoint his brother Li Liu grand general who pacifies the east so both wings secure the realm.
proposals.after: Li Te had troop supervisor Li Han of the six commanderies, Shanggui prefect Ren Zang, Shichang prefect Yan Shi, counsellor Li Pan, Chencang prefect Li Wu, Yinping prefect Li Yuan, and commandant Yang Bao memorialize the throne, citing the precedent of Liang Tong's support for Dou Rong: appoint Li Te acting grand general who pacifies the north with authority to enfeoff and appoint on the emperor's behalf, and appoint his younger brother Li Liu acting general who pacifies the east, so that the two might jointly hold command.
proposals.reason: 其弟流行鎮東將軍 is acting General Who Pacifies the East, not a grand general (contrast 行鎮北大將軍 for Li Te); 弟 is younger brother; 依梁統奉竇融故事 is the precedent of Liang Tong supporting/elevating Dou Rong, not 'presenting' him; 承制封拜 is enfeoffing and appointing on imperial authority; 以相鎮統 is joint command, not 'both wings secure the realm'. All twelve name occurrences keep the same order.

proposals.before: When Li Te exercised imperial mandate he named Li Liu grand general who pacifies the east, stationed him in the eastern camp, and titled him chief protector of the east.
proposals.after: When Li Te exercised authority on the emperor's behalf he named Li Liu general who pacifies the east, stationed him in the eastern camp, and styled him Eastern Protector.
proposals.reason: 以流為鎮東將軍 is General Who Pacifies the East, not a grand general (the literal correctly has Pacify-East general); 號為東督護 is a style, 'Eastern Protector', without 'chief'. Names unchanged.

proposals.before: Elder brother Fu was nimble-cavalry general; younger brother Xiang was fierce-cavalry general; eldest son Shi was awe-inspiring martial general; second son Dang was garrison general; youngest son Xiong was forward general; Li Han was Western Yi colonel—Han sons Guoli, Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, Fei Tuo etc. were commanders; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, Qu Xin etc. were claws-and-fangs; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, Wang Huai etc. were staff; Yan Shi was plot master; He Shi, Zhao Su were belly-hearts.
proposals.after: Elder brother Fu was nimble-cavalry general; younger brother Xiang was fierce-cavalry general; eldest son Shi was awe-inspiring martial general; second son Dang was garrison general; youngest son Xiong was forward general; Li Han was Western Yi colonel—Han sons Guo and Li, Ren Hui, Li Gong, Shangguan Jing, Li Pan, Fei Tuo etc. were commanders; Ren Zang, Shangguan Dun, Yang Bao, Yang Gui, Wang Da, Qu Xin etc. were claws-and-fangs; Li Yuan, Li Bo, Xi Bin, Yan Cheng, Shangguan Qi, Li Tao, Wang Huai etc. were staff; Yan Shi was plot master; He Shi, Zhao Su were belly-hearts.
proposals.reason: Paired-field completion of accepted repair jinshu:120:r0010 and claim retraction c0268: 含子國離 is two sons, Guo and Li (s0200 含子離 confirms Li Li). The idiomatic field was corrected but the literal still fuses them as 'Guoli'.

proposals.before: When Yan Shi arrived he saw Xin Ran palisading vital crossings to ambush refugees and sighed: "Building fortifications without invaders means someone plans a massacre.
proposals.after: When Yan Shi arrived he saw Xin Ran palisading vital crossings and plotting to ambush the refugees, and sighed: "To build walls where there are no invaders is to raise works the enemy will surely occupy.
proposals.reason: Paired-field completion of accepted repair r0008: 無寇而城，仇必保焉 (a Zuozhuan saying) means the enemy will surely occupy works built where there is no war; the reviewer already rejected 'slaughter/massacre' for the literal, but the idiomatic still says 'someone plans a massacre'. 謀掩流人 is restored as Xin Ran's plot. Names unchanged.

proposals.before: Though Master Liu is your uncle, desperate times grant no gentleness—your father depends on you; what further excuse remains?"
proposals.after: Though Master Liu is your uncle, circumstances leave no choice; as for my own old father, I leave him to you—what more is there to say?"
proposals.reason: 老父在君 is Li Li speaking of his own father Li Han (the second of the 二翁 in s0201): 'my old father is in your hands'. Li Xiong's father Li Te is already dead (s0175), so 'your father depends on you' misattributes the kinship; 勢不得已 is 'circumstances leave no choice'. 'Master Liu' is kept unchanged.

proposals.before: Across Ba and Shu the people walled every hilltop; towns stood empty, Li Liu found nothing left to forage in the open country, and his troops starved.
proposals.after: Across the Three Shu commanderies the people held the strongpoints and built fortified villages; towns stood empty, Li Liu found nothing left to forage in the open country, and his troops starved.
proposals.reason: 三蜀 is the Three Shu (Shu, Guanghan and Qianwei commanderies), not Ba and Shu; 保險結塢 is holding strongpoints and building fortified villages. Li Liu unchanged.

proposals.before: The Li brothers are formidable; we are about to be toyed with like boys.
proposals.after: The Li brothers are men of heroic talent; we are about to become captives of these upstarts.
proposals.reason: 吾屬將為豎子虜矣 is 'we will become the captives of these brats', not 'toyed with like boys'; 並有雄才 is heroic talent (claim already reads 'heroic talent'). 'The Li brothers' is kept unchanged.

proposals.before: He also wrote Li Te's major Shangguan Dun to insist that accepting surrender must never resemble indulging the foe.
proposals.after: He also wrote to Li Te's major Shangguan Dun, earnestly arguing that those who surrender should be received as warily as one awaits an enemy.
proposals.reason: 深陳納降若待敵之義 is the principle that accepting surrender should be handled as if facing an enemy (i.e. with vigilance), not that it must 'never resemble indulging the foe'. Names unchanged.

proposals.before: Li Xiang was a seasoned Eastern Qiang commander who knew regulations by heart; he needed no signal drums—lifting his spear aligned the ranks—and executed three unruly soldiers until his formation stood rigid as iron.
proposals.after: Li Xiang had long been a fine commander among the Eastern Qiang and knew military law; he used no banners or pennants—lifting his spear aligned the ranks—and executed three subordinates who disobeyed orders, so that his formation stood in strict order.
proposals.reason: 不用麾幟 is 'did not use banners/pennants', not signal drums; 斬部下不用命者三人 is three subordinates who disobeyed orders; 素東羌良將 is 'had long been a fine commander of the Eastern Qiang'. Li Xiang unchanged.

proposals.before: Zhao Xin resented such disciplined popularity and plotted murder without breathing a word.
proposals.after: Zhao Xin resented such discipline and wished to kill him, but did not yet say so.
proposals.reason: 廞惡其齊整，欲殺之而未言: Zhao Xin hated his orderliness and wished to kill him but had not spoken; 'popularity' is not in the source. Zhao Xin unchanged.

proposals.before: Zhao Xin flushed with staged wrath: "What minister may utter such words?"
proposals.after: Zhao Xin said angrily: "How can a subject say such things?"
proposals.reason: 廞怒曰 is simply 'Zhao Xin said angrily'; 'staged wrath' is an unsupported interpretive addition about his motive. 此豈人臣所宜言 is 'how can this be what a subject should say'. Zhao Xin unchanged.

proposals.before: Li Te secretly rallied seven thousand fighters, struck Fei Yuan by night, shattered his host, and set the camps ablaze so that nine in ten died.
proposals.after: Li Te secretly rallied more than seven thousand fighters, struck Fei Yuan by night, shattered his host, and set the camps ablaze so that eight or nine in ten died.
proposals.reason: 死者十八九 is eight or nine in ten (claim already says 'eight or nine tenths'); 七千餘人 is more than seven thousand. Names unchanged.

proposals.before: Luo Shang's army dissolved; barely one man in ten escaped.
proposals.after: Luo Shang's army fell into disorder; only one or two in ten made it back.
proposals.reason: 敗還者十一二: those who returned in defeat were one or two in ten (the literal already says one-two tenths). Luo Shang unchanged.

proposals.before: Shu prefect Xu Jian yielded the lesser citadel; Li Te installed Li Jin to pacify the district.
proposals.after: Shu prefect Xu Jian surrendered the lesser city; Li Te made Li Jin prefect of Shu commandery to pacify it.
proposals.reason: 特以李瑾為蜀郡太守 states the office Li Jin received (claim p120 office 'Shu prefect'); the idiomatic omitted it. 小城 is the lesser city. Names unchanged in order.

proposals.before: When the refugees first reached Hanzhong they petitioned for permission to winter in Ba and Shu; the court refused and dispatched Censor Li Bi with imperial credentials to console them while keeping watch—and barred them from crossing Jiange Pass.
proposals.after: When the refugees first reached Hanzhong they petitioned to be allowed to seek sustenance in Ba and Shu; the court refused and dispatched Censor Li Bi with imperial credentials to console them while keeping watch—and barred them from crossing Jiange Pass.
proposals.reason: 求寄食巴、蜀 is a request to lodge and find food in Ba and Shu; 'to winter' adds an unsupported season. Names unchanged.

proposals.before: For his role in defeating Zhao Xin the court named Li Te general who proclaims might and lord of Changle village, while Li Liu became general who rouses might and marquis of Wuyang.
proposals.after: For his role in defeating Zhao Xin the court named Li Te general who proclaims might and enfeoffed him as marquis of Changle village, while Li Liu became general who rouses might and marquis of Wuyang.
proposals.reason: 封長樂鄉侯 is enfeoffment as a marquis (侯), parallel to Li Liu's 武陽侯 in the same sentence; 'lord' hides the rank and the enfeoffment. Names unchanged.

proposals.before: Xin Ran had been promoted out of turn yet ignored recall orders and hoped to credit himself alone with Zhao Xin's destruction, so he suppressed the court's dispatch and reported falsely.
proposals.after: Xin Ran had been summoned out of sequence but ignored the summons, and he hoped to claim sole credit for destroying Zhao Xin, so he suppressed the court's order and did not report the facts.
proposals.reason: 會辛冉以非次見征，不顧應召: 非次見征 is an irregular (out-of-sequence) summons and 不顧應召 is ignoring that summons, not a promotion plus 'recall orders'; 不以實上 is failing to report the facts. Names Xin Ran and Zhao Xin unchanged.

proposals.before: Te ordered six commanderies men troop supervisors Li Han, Shanggui magistrate Ren Zang, Shichang magistrate Yan Shi, grandee consultant Li Pan, Chencang magistrate Li Wu, Yinping magistrate Li Yuan, commandant of troops Yang Bao etc. memorialize; beg according to Liang Tong submitting Dou Rong precedent—lift Te acting Pacify-North grand general, inherit regulations enfeoff appoint—his younger brother Liu act Pacify-East general—to mutually anchor command.
proposals.after: Te ordered the six commanderies' troop supervisor Li Han, Shanggui magistrate Ren Zang, Shichang magistrate Yan Shi, consultant grandee Li Pan, Chencang magistrate Li Wu, Yinping magistrate Li Yuan, and commandant of troops Yang Bao and others to memorialize; they requested, following the precedent of Liang Tong supporting Dou Rong, that Te be advanced as acting Grand General Who Pacifies the North, empowered to enfeoff and appoint on the emperor's behalf, and his younger brother Liu as acting General Who Pacifies the East, so they might jointly hold command.
proposals.reason: Paired-field completion of the accepted s0118 idiomatic repair: 梁統奉竇融 is Liang Tong supporting Dou Rong (奉 = support, not 'submitting'); 承制封拜 is enfeoffing and appointing on delegated imperial authority, not 'inherit regulations'; 行鎮東將軍 is a general, not a grand general; 六郡人部曲督 is one office held by Li Han.

proposals.before: When Te inherited regulations—made Liu Pacify-East general—dwelt east camp—styled East Protector chief.
proposals.after: When Te exercised authority on the emperor's behalf—made Liu General Who Pacifies the East—stationed him in the east camp—styled him Eastern Protector.
proposals.reason: Paired-field completion of the accepted s0184 idiomatic repair: 特之承制也 is Li Te exercising delegated imperial authority, not 'inherited regulations'; 號為東督護 contains no 'chief'.

proposals.before: Hu elder-brother Han son Li heard father wished surrender—from Zitong galloped back—wished remonstrate not reach—withdrew with Xiong plotted raid Fu army—said: If merit accomplished affair aided—covenant with you three years alternate be lord.
proposals.after: Hu's elder brother, Han's son Li, heard his father wished to surrender—from Zitong galloped back—wished to remonstrate but did not arrive in time—withdrew with Xiong and plotted a raid on Fu's army—said: If merit is accomplished and the affair succeeds—I covenant with you to alternate as lord every three years.
proposals.reason: 胡兄含子離 identifies Li Li as Li Hu's elder brother and Li Han's son; the literal garbled that preserved kinship. 欲諫不及 is arriving too late to remonstrate; 約與君三年迭為主 is a covenant to alternate as lord every three years.

proposals.before: For punish rebel Qiang merit—memorialized Xiang as awe-bandit general—lent crimson canopy curved umbrella—enfeoffed Yangquan village marquis—granted cash million—horses fifty.
proposals.after: For merit in punishing the rebel Qiang—memorialized Xiang as General Who Awes Bandits—granted temporary use of a crimson banner and curved canopy—enfeoffed him Marquis of Yangquan Village—granted one million cash and fifty horses.
proposals.reason: 假赤幢曲蓋 is a temporary grant of two insignia, a crimson banner (赤幢) and a curved canopy (曲蓋), not one 'crimson canopy curved umbrella'; 威寇將軍 and 陽泉亭侯 rendered as titles.

proposals.after: As Luo Shang withdrew, Li Te pursued through more than thirty li of fighting until Luo Shang threw his main force forward and broke him. Luo Shang's troops beheaded Li Te, Li Fu, and Li Yuan, burned their bodies, and sent their heads to Luoyang.
